briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Threats and Emergency Warnings
sections.content: Today's news once again highlights the severity of the global climate crisis. In Nepal, a major flood warning led to a complex disaster, demonstrating the ongoing impacts of climate change [1]. Domestically, 'Bukang-i' appearing in Busan's North Port is being interpreted as a symbol warning of the climate crisis [7]. Experts' warnings that water and food shortages are directly linked to climate change were re-emphasized [30, 64], and concerns were raised about the impact of climate change on daily life, such as damage to household medicines or a significant portion of heatwave-related emergency room visits in the Triad region [34, 56]. In particular, the outgoing UN Secretary-General strongly warned that polluters are treating the atmosphere like an 'open sewer,' and humanity faces an unprecedented threat [43, 69, 70, 74]. Rising sea levels pose an 'existential threat' to humanity, heritage, and nature [75], and direct damage cases, such as the permanent closure of ski resorts due to climate change in Austria, were also reported [46].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Diplomacy and Policy Debates
sections.content: On the UN stage today, various international discussions and conflicting perspectives regarding climate change were expressed. President Lee, in his UN keynote address, emphasized international cooperation by proposing a 'K-Initiative solution' for AI, climate change, and energy supply chain issues [5]. In contrast, former President Donald Trump showed a different approach, opposing AI regulation and drawing parallels with climate change [32, 51, 73]. With the COP31 summit approaching, international attention is focused, with Turkey's Minister of Environment presenting the agenda [59, 67]. However, reports that clean energy commitments were omitted from COP31's electrification pledge and that the UN climate change body is criticized for conflicts of interest and the influence of specific countries suggest challenges in international climate governance [57, 63]. Furthermore, diverse viewpoints were presented, such as the argument that climate change is the world's most exaggerated problem [60] and an editor's opinion that it is 'insane' for companies to consider climate change only as a long-term risk [58], demonstrating that differences in perception regarding climate change still persist.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Underlying Warnings
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to achieve carbon neutrality are ongoing. Jeong Hak-geun, the new president of the Korea Institute of Energy Research, emphasized a major R&D transformation and leap forward for carbon neutrality upon his inauguration [8, 9, 12]. Korea District Heating Corporation is strengthening ESG management, including on-site inspections for carbon neutrality [11], and Nubo showcased carbon-neutral agricultural technologies at the Busan EXPO [13]. Gwangmyeong City and Okcheon County are each promoting carbon neutrality in daily life by establishing five-year environmental education plans and recruiting households to participate in the carbon neutrality points system [14, 16]. However, despite these efforts, the news that Korea's greenhouse gas emissions decreased by 0.9% but 'net emissions' increased, signaling a warning light for achieving carbon reduction targets, indicates the need for deep reflection on current approaches [17].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: Policy and technological advancements to accelerate the transition to renewable energy are being reported. The '1km barrier' siting regulation for solar power generation facilities has been removed, paving the way for expanded renewable energy deployment [21]. KEPCO E&C is actively engaging in public-private partnerships, including developing technology-finance linked renewable energy projects [20]. Jeju High-Tech Industrial Complex is transforming into an innovation hub for renewable energy and clean bio [24], and Jeonnam Information & Culture Industry Promotion Agency is also striving to cultivate future talent by recruiting free practical trainees for 'Renewable Energy × AI' [22]. However, simultaneously, the severe shortage of personnel in the renewable energy sector, particularly with an approval rate of only 17.5% for increased staffing, is highlighted as a significant obstacle to sustainable growth [19]. Furthermore, amid surging power demand from AI data centers, calls have emerged to limit power supply to renewable energy, and warnings have been raised that a significant portion of data center plans may be speculative [23, 29].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Change Adaptation, Innovation, and Public Awareness
sections.content: Diverse efforts are continuing to adapt to climate change and raise public awareness. Seoul's Seongdong District is creating 'Seongdong's Seasons,' a garden designed to be resilient to climate change, aiming to enhance urban climate resilience [2]. Jeonnam Gwangju Agricultural Research & Extension Services is also actively engaged in agricultural adaptation efforts, such as developing a peach management model in response to climate change [6]. The awards ceremony for the 'Climate Change Response Project Contest' for youth [3] and activities exploring climate change and future careers on weather observation vessels [4] are becoming important opportunities to raise climate awareness among future generations. Furthermore, characters like 'Captain Noah: Climate Change Superhero' are being introduced to attract public interest [49, 61], and a brochure providing a reliable guide to climate change information has been published in Canada [65]. News that New York City is preparing for climate change demonstrates urban-level adaptation efforts [38], while phenomena such as wine's alcohol content strengthening due to climate change and extreme heat [50, 55], or the perspective of wasp spiders found in northern England as 'climate refugees' [71], highlight the importance of adaptation and observation of ecosystem changes.

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we have examined the severity of the global climate crisis, alongside policy debates within the international community, domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition, and various attempts at climate change adaptation. While maintaining vigilance against climate threats, we must simultaneously continue innovation and practical actions for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: An adult wasp spider (Argiope bruennichi), originally native to mainland Europe, North Africa, and Asia, has been spotted for the first time in Cheshire, Northwest Britain. This species has rarely been seen in the north and west of Britain.
